NK cells engineered with a chimeric antigen receptor delay HIV rebound and reshape HIV reservoir composition
articles.abstract: Abstract Durable HIV remission requires strategies that eliminate or permanently silence the latent reservoir that persists despite antiretroviral therapy (ART). We engineer allogeneic human primary natural killer (NK) cells expressing a truncated CD4-based chimeric antigen receptor (D1D2 CAR) targeting the conserved CD4 binding site on HIV Env. D1D2 CAR NK cells selectively kill HIV-infected primary CD4 T cells in vitro and significantly delay viral rebound following ART interruption in humanized mice infected with barcoded CCR5-tropic HIV. Barcoded HIV tracking shows reductions in the number and diversity of rebounding viral RNA lineages, together with decreased inter-organ sharing of rebound-associated proviral barcodes and integration sites. Integration site and chromatin analyses suggest that rebound-associated proviruses remaining after D1D2 CAR-NK treatment are less frequently located in genic and transcriptionally active chromatin contexts. Thus, CAR-NK cells may target reactivating HIV-infected cells during early ART interruption and shape the composition of the reservoir contributing to rebound.

articles.title: Omnidirectional photonic chiral flatband in nonlocal membrane metasurfaces
Melanosome evolution shaped sensory biology and terrestrial adaptations in early aquatic vertebrates
articles.abstract: Abstract The photic environment is a key driver of fish ecology that shapes adaptations to aquatic habitats. The evolutionary history of these adaptations, however, is difficult to trace. Melanosomes, melanin-rich organelles, offer unique insights into physiology and ecology and often fossilise. Here, we present a comparative analysis of melanosomes from extant and fossil fishes to trace the evolution of ecological and physiological adaptations through deep time. Melanosomes from internal tissues of extant fishes exhibit highly conserved geometries in all major taxonomic groups examined, indicating persistent functional constraints during evolution. Larger, more abundant melanosomes in lungfish likely reflect adaptations that underpin the vertebrate water-to-land transition. In contrast, eye melanosomes exhibit lineage-specific patterns. Bony fishes possess cylindrical eye melanosomes associated with retinomotor movements, photoreceptor protection, and improved visual acuity, whereas jawless and cartilaginous fishes possess only spheroidal melanosomes, consistent with visual sensitivity and alternative light-regulation strategies including pupillary modulation. These taxonomic differences are preserved in fossils from the late Carboniferous Mazon Creek biota, indicating that links between melanosome morphology and function were established during the early evolutionary history of these lineages in the Ordovician, approximately 445 million years ago. Early innovations in melanin biology uniquely facilitated vertebrate sensory evolution and ecological diversification.

articles.title: Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease
DEGS1-mTORC1-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming fuels rhabdomyosarcoma progression and unveils a therapeutic vulnerability
Evaluation of vaccine-induced anti-lipopolysaccharide antibodies against clinically relevant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains to inform vaccine design
articles.abstract: Abstract Klebsiella pneumoniae is a leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and is increasingly multi-drug resistant, highlighting the need for vaccines. Putative vaccine targets include the lipopolysaccharide (O antigen) and capsular polysaccharide (K antigen), but capsule may mask O antigen and limit antibody-mediated opsonophagocytosis. We evaluated the activity of O antigen-specific antibodies induced by a tetravalent bioconjugate vaccine against 146 clinical isolates representing 17 prevalent capsule types associated with neonatal sepsis. Susceptibility to antibody-mediated killing varied by capsule type: four were consistently susceptible, six showed heterogeneous responses, and seven were resistant despite remaining susceptible to K antigen-specific antibodies. Killing of susceptible strains was predominantly mediated by anti-O1 antibodies, as demonstrated by competitive inhibition with purified polysaccharides. Collectively, these findings support an antigen-sparing vaccine design strategy, in which susceptible capsule types may be replaced by a single O type, reducing vaccine complexity while maintaining broad functional coverage.

articles.title: Ultra-low loss piezo-optomechanical low-confinement silicon nitride platform for visible wavelength quantum photonic circuits
articles.abstract: Abstract Realizing photonic quantum computing at scale requires integrated circuits that combine ultra-low loss with fast, low-power, low-hysteresis, and low-crosstalk reconfiguration. These requirements are particularly challenging at visible wavelengths, where many quantum resource-state generators, including single-photon sources and quantum memories, naturally operate. Low-confinement silicon nitride waveguides offer the requisite loss performance, but conventional thermo-optic modulators dissipate significant static power, driving thermal crosstalk and precluding cryogenic operation. Visible-wavelength piezo-optomechanical circuits avoid these drawbacks, but existing demonstrations rely either on high-confinement waveguides with propagation losses of 35-100 dB/m, or on low-confinement platforms using foundry-incompatible lead zirconate titanate (PZT). Here we combine piezo-optomechanical actuation with a CMOS-foundry-fabricated, low-confinement silicon nitride platform, achieving 2.6 dB/m propagation loss at 780 nm, megahertz-scale modulation bandwidth, a half-wave voltage-length product of 2.8 V ⋅ m, and negligible hysteresis. We demonstrate reconfigurable Mach-Zehnder interferometers with 0.63 dB loss per spiral phase shifter, enabling deep, actively reconfigurable visible-wavelength quantum photonic circuits.

articles.title: A SARS-CoV-2 entry inhibitor trimerizes to lock the spike protein in a closed conformation
articles.abstract: Abstract The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds its receptor ACE2 to initiate target-cell infection. To engage ACE2, at least one of the three receptor-binding domains (RBDs) of the spike must adopt the up orientation. Here, we describe S22, a potent, bioavailable, and non-toxic inhibitor of BA.2 and all subsequent Omicron variants. Cryo-EM analyses showed that S22 assembled as a trimer in the central cavity of the spike apex, stabilizing all three RBDs in the down orientation, thereby preventing ACE2 association. Binding studies, especially those using mixed S22-sensitive and -resistant spikes, imply a cooperative assembly of three S22 molecules with three RBDs, resulting in an unusually slow S22 off-rate. Consistent with its slow dissociation and favorable pharmacokinetics, S22 suppressed viral replication and inflammation in the lungs of XBB.1.5-infected female mice. Thus, S22 potently inhibits Omicron entry through a distinct mechanism whereby a small compound assembles cooperatively as a trimer to stabilize spike in an inactive conformation.

articles.title: Marine heat waves in vulnerable coral reef regions are skillfully predictable on multi-year timescales
Inflammatory memory primes the intestine for enhanced regenerative potential
Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels
articles.abstract: Abstract Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Brazil accounted for 70% of dengue cases reported worldwide in 2024, and the virus has recently become endemic in the southernmost state of Rio Grande do Sul. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. During this period, Aedes aegypti expanded across state municipalities, with a marked increase in dengue cases from 2020 onward. Nearly half of the municipalities surpassed the incidence threshold of ≥20 cases per 100,000 residents per year by 2023, indicating endemic transmission. Genomic analysis of 665 new DENV genomes is consistent with the local persistence of viral lineages across years, driving seasonal outbreaks. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. These findings highlight the north-to-south expansion of dengue into temperate regions, emphasizing the urgent need for intensification of vector control and surveillance in newly endemic areas to mitigate dengue burden in a mostly naive human population.

articles.title: Tuning ferroptosis-like, cancer-selective cell death with charge-imbalanced nanoparticles
articles.abstract: Abstract It is known that nanoparticles functionalized with mixed charge monolayers – that is, monolayers composed of both positively [+] and negatively [-] charged ligands – can induce selective death of cancer cells. Remarkably, however, when the ligand polarities and proportions are kept constant, but the chemical nature of the “minority” [-] component is altered, the nanoparticles exhibit distinct intracellular localization patterns and induce different forms of iron-dependent lipid-peroxidation-driven cell death, which we term “ferroptosis-like” due to concurrent activation of caspases. In particular, changing the end groups on the [-] ligands from carboxylic to sulfonic to phosphonic acid shifts nanoparticle accumulation from lysosomes to autophagic compartments to late endosomes, respectively. These distinct cellular outcomes are accompanied by marked differences in the composition of serum protein coronas adsorbed onto the mixed-charge nanoparticles. Proteomic analysis revealed exceedingly complex corona proteomes, comprising more than 800 different proteins, many enriched hundreds- to thousands-fold compared to blood serum, with numerous proteins selectively enriched on specific nanoparticle types. Together, these findings identify charge-imbalanced constructs as potential modulators of subcellular organelle targeting and ferroptosis-like cell death.

articles.title: scBOA: Bayesian optimization of single-cell analysis pipelines for robust annotation and discovery
Distinct conformational states of HSV-2 gH/gL captured by cryoEM reveal structural principles governing fusion activation
articles.abstract: Abstract Orthoherpesviridae infect most humans for life and cause myriad diseases. These viruses distribute cell-entry functions among receptor-binding proteins such as gD, the conserved membrane fusogen gB, and the gH/gL heterodimer, which couples receptor engagement to gB activation. Here, we report cryoEM structures of HSV-2 gH/gL, including complexes with four antibody fragments, in distinct conformational states. Structural analysis suggests that these structures represent pre-activation and intermediate states rather than a post-activation state. Antibody binding appears to shift the gH/gL conformational equilibrium of gH/gL, either stabilizing the pre-activation state or promoting refolding into intermediate or post-activation-like states. Two regions – the N terminus and a domain H2 switch – adopt distinct conformations and may transmit the activating signal from gD to gB. We propose that receptor-bound gD displaces the gH N terminus, initiating allosteric rearrangements that culminate in switch refolding and may help release prefusion gB from an autoinhibited gH/gL-gB complex. Switch conservation suggests that this activation mechanism may be shared across Orthoherpesviridae . These findings uncover structural principles governing gH/gL-mediated activation of membrane fusion.

articles.title: Synthesis-by-design of ferroelectric Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites
articles.abstract: Abstract Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites are promising ferroelectric materials, combining chemically tunable polarity enabled by their organic spacers with enhanced environmental stability. However, rational discovery remains difficult owing to uncertain phase formability and scarce, biased ferroelectric data. Here we show a staged, physically guided synthesis-by-design workflow that integrates learning from scarce ferroelectric data with structure-aware screening. Starting from 11 known ferroelectric compounds in this family, symbolic regression defines a descriptor-bounded ferroelectric-consistent region. Similarity-guided expansion and chemical filtering reduce 83,924 molecules to 1012 candidate divalent spacers, while machine-learned interatomic-potential relaxation and connectivity analysis identify 338 candidates retaining Dion–Jacobson connectivity. Sequential prioritization by connectivity retention, chemical similarity, energetic refinement and synthetic accessibility selects s −2-fluorobutane-1,4-diamine, leading to the synthesis of a PbI 4 -based Dion–Jacobson perovskite with experimentally confirmed ferroelectric switching. This prospective proof of concept shows how sparse property knowledge can be coupled with structural screening to prioritize organic spacer candidates for experimental synthesis.

articles.title: Nascent RNA-mediated recruitment and R-loop suppression underlie FUS-driven enhancement of transcription
Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information

Soil
Heating from
Fire Induces Bidirectional Changes
in Dissolved Organic Matter Release and Organic Sulfur Speciation
articles.abstract: Abstract Soil heating from fire influences dissolved organic matter (DOM) release but has unknown effects on organic sulfur (S) speciation, with implications for S and metal cycling in aquatic environments. Here, low and high organic carbon soils (4.80 versus 50.4%) were heated at environmentally relevant temperatures and durations (75–300 °C, 0.25–4.0 h) and subject to leaching experiments that quantified DOM and inorganic anion release, and changes in organic S speciation via S X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy. In both soils, heating between 75 and 200 °C increased dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and inorganic sulfate (SO42–) release (by up to 24- and 88-fold, respectively) while decreasing the % highly reduced S in DOM (e.g., thiols), indicating thiol oxidation to SO42–. Soil heating at 300 °C decreased DOC release and increased SO42– release, with step increases in DOM aromaticity and % heterocyclic reduced S species (e.g., thiophenes). Across treatments, DOM aromaticity positively correlated with DOM % heterocyclic reduced S, interpreted to reflect organic S cyclization during heating. The observed bidirectional changes in organic S speciation in DOM due to soil heating, with thiol oxidation at ≤200 °C and S cyclization at 300 °C with SO42– releases, provide mechanistic insights that improve the prediction of fire effects on S, C, and metal cycling in aquatic environments.

articles.title:
Correction to “Nitrous
Oxide Emissions from
Urban Green Spaces Substantially Offset Their Carbon Sequestration
Benefits”

Recombinase Polymerase
Amplification Coupled with
Graphene Oxide Nanomaterial-Assisted Purification and Target Signal
Selection for Highly Sensitive and Rapid Harmful Algae Detection
articles.abstract: Abstract Harmful algal blooms (HABs) pose serious ecological and health risks, creating an urgent need for rapid, sensitive, and accurate detection of harmful algae. Here, we developed a graphene oxide (GO)- and Mg2+-regulated recombinase polymerase amplification assay (G-M-RPA) for rapid and ultrasensitive detection of Heterosigma akashiwo, Prorocentrum minimum, and Akashiwo sanguinea. Using conserved internal transcribed spacer sequences, we designed species-specific primers labeled with 6-carboxyfluorescein for fluorescence readout. Innovative one-step purification of RPA products was achieved using self-synthesized GO-wrapped magnetic nanocomposites instead of traditional purification kits, reducing purification time from 15 to 2 min (∼86.7%). The fluorescence resonance energy transfer property of the GO nanosheets was applied to quench the fluorescence of excess single-stranded primers, significantly lowering background levels. Mg2+ further enhanced primer–GO interactions, likely through electrostatic screening and Mg2+-mediated interactions. The entire detection process was completed within ∼30 min, achieving a genomic DNA detection limit of 3.3 fg/μL, corresponding to ∼7 cells/mL for H. akashiwo. The assay also showed reliable performance in mixed-DNA and seawater matrices, with favorable reproducibility and short-term stability. Overall, the proposed G-M-RPA strategy provides a rapid, sensitive, and practical platform for multispecies harmful-algae detection, nearshore environmental monitoring, and early warning of HABs.

articles.title:
Observation-Based
Emission Estimates of the Potent
Greenhouse Gas HFC-23 for Article 5 and Non-Article 5 Country Groups
under the Montreal Protocol
articles.abstract: Abstract The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol requires parties to destroy, to the extent practicable, HFC-23 generated as a byproduct during the production of controlled hydrochlorofluorocarbons and hydrofluorocarbons. Global total HFC-23 emissions estimated from reported abatement and known sources (bottom-up) agreed with those inferred from atmospheric observations (top-down) before 2015, but have been substantially lower since then. Here, we show that during 2011–2013, bottom-up estimates of global total HFC-23 emissions were right for the wrong reasons: bottom-up estimates for the non-Article 5 (mainly developed) country group were lower than top-down estimates (1.7 ± 0.2 vs 3.1 ± 0.5 Gg yr–1 on average), while those for the Article 5 (mainly developing) country group were higher (11.8 ± 0.4 vs 9.7 ± 1.0 Gg yr–1), resulting in a cancellation at the global scale. We further show that during 2015–2023, while the underestimation of global bottom-up emissions was dominated by the Article 5 country group, the non-Article 5 country group also contributed in 2023 [bottom-up (byproduct emissions reported to UNEP plus other known sources) vs top-down: 0.5 ± 0.2 vs 1.3 ± 0.6 Gg yr–1]. Our results underscore improvement of emission accounting and mitigation for both country groups under the Kigali Amendment.

articles.title:
Celebrating the
30th Anniversary of the Department
of Environmental Science and Engineering, Fudan University
Trace H2O2-triggered Fenton-like reaction by secondary coordination sphere in iron-based metal-organic frameworks
MoS2-based composites with magnetoelectric synergistic loss for enhanced microwave absorption
articles.abstract: Abstract The development of high-performance electromagnetic wave absorbing materials is crucial for addressing electromagnetic interference issues. However, a single loss mechanism often results in unsatisfactory microwave absorption performance. In this study, we report a MoS 2 -based composite material with a magnetoelectric synergistic effect. The hierarchical heterogeneous structure and the synergistic loss of magnetic/electric components enable excellent impedance matching and multiple energy conversions, enhancing the absorption and loss capabilities. The designed microwave absorber achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 4.36 GHz at a thickness of 1.9 mm. The minimum reflection loss is −58.92 dB. Furthermore, the absorber exhibits a radar cross-section reduction value of up to 28.273 dB·m² in the vertical direction. Additionally, the EAB can be further broadened across the entire 2-18 GHz frequency range through the rational design of gradient metamaterials. This work provides a reference for the subsequent development and application of MoS 2 -based composites with high-efficiency electromagnetic wave absorption properties.

articles.title: Association of fetal activity patterns in utero with postnatal sleep behavior
articles.abstract: Abstract The human circadian clock, a key mechanism governing the sleep-wake cycle, starts oscillating before birth. Distinct fetal behavioral states have been described using short-duration ultrasound recordings, but the alignment of fetal activity with day and night cycles (i.e., diurnal rhythms) remains poorly understood due to the lack of long-term monitoring. This study characterizes fetal diurnal activity patterns using continuous third-trimester monitoring over at least five days across 32 mother-child pairs, yielding over 20,000 combined sensor-hours of maternal (acceleration and temperature) and fetal (acceleration) wearable data. We tracked diurnal pattern development from in utero to 6 months of age, assessing infant sleep at three postnatal time points (first weeks, 3 months, and 6 months) with sleep diaries and questionnaires. Multi-level modeling revealed early diurnal rhythms in fetuses that align with maternal activity and circadian rhythms. Random Forest analyses identified fetal day/night sleep duration ratio – a simplified proxy for fetal circadian entrainment – as the strongest predictor of postnatal infant sleep, with fetuses preferring nighttime sleep maintaining this preference postnatally. Maternal sleep regularity (i.e., consistent sleep patterns characterized by low day-to-day variability in sleep timing) during pregnancy also predicted infant sleep, being associated with a stronger preference for nighttime sleep in infants. These findings highlight the potential influence of intrauterine and maternal factors on early circadian entrainment and highlight maternal sleep as an actionable target to improve infant sleep and family well-being. A limitation of this study is the relatively small cohort size and, consequently, the findings should be interpreted with caution until they are replicated in larger, independent cohorts.

articles.title: Engineered d-p orbital hybridization unlocks dilute CO2 electrolysis to byproduct-free CH4-rich syngas

Mechanistic Understanding
of Breath-Borne Bacterial
Inactivation Kinetics in Oxidant-Rich and Natural Air
articles.abstract: Abstract Bioaerosols play a central role in respiratory infection transmission, but how atmospheric oxidants affect their viability, especially in human respiratory fluids, remains unexplored. Here, we investigated the inactivation of five bacterial species with distinct cell envelope architectures (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Bacillus subtilis, Staphylococcus aureus, and Mycobacterium smegmatis) suspended in human exhaled breath condensate (EBC) droplets exposed to gas-phase hydroxyl radicals (•OH) produced by ultraviolet irradiation of H2O2. Compared with the other three exposure conditions, the •OH-generating (H2O2+UV) treatment caused the greatest viability loss, with 4-h survival ranging from 24.3% (E. coli) to 63.0% (M. smegmatis). Gram-negative bacteria were sensitive to both H2O2 and •OH, whereas Gram-positive species resisted H2O2 but were inactivated by •OH. M. smegmatis showed the highest tolerance. Inactivation accelerated in smaller droplets, and the size-dependent kinetics were characterized using Weibull and first-order models incorporating surface-area-to-volume ratio. Morphological, biochemical, and metabolomic analyses indicated that the observed inactivation differences were associated with bacterial envelope types and surface characteristics. •OH preferentially degrades outer membrane glycolipids in Gram-negative bacteria and oxidizes cytoplasmic membrane lipids in Gram-positive bacteria, while all species shared a core signature of nucleic acid oxidative damage. These findings provide a molecular understanding of bacterial inactivation kinetics in human EBC droplets and may inform the assessment of bioaerosol transmission risks.

articles.title:
Near-Complete Decomposition
of Soil Microplastics
over Transient Electrical Heating and Associated Benefits
articles.abstract: Abstract Soil serves as a significant sink for microplastics, posing considerable risks to both the ecological and human health. The diverse composition and dynamic transformation of microplastics present major challenges for remediation as conventional strategies often fail to achieve efficient and complete decomposition. In this study, biochar was applied to microplastic-contaminated soil as a conductive material to initiate transient electric heating under a low-power input. This approach facilitated near-complete decomposition of soil microplastics (>95.0%) across the tested soil and microplastic types while preventing soil hardening. Specifically, electric heating enhanced interactions between soil microplastics and the biochar conductor, leading to the formation of highly aromatic carbon (HAC). The resulting HAC not only improved soil microecology but also supported the growth of pak choi (Brassica campestris L. ssp.). The newly formed HAC was found to upregulate the expression of auxin-responsive gene families, including Aux/IAA and GH3, in the roots. HAC enriched tryptamine in the rhizosphere, and tryptamine abundance was positively correlated with the relative abundance of Sphingomonas, a genus with a reported capacity to convert tryptamine-derived intermediates toward indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) biosynthesis. These findings demonstrate that transient electric heating offers a sustainable strategy for decomposing diverse soil microplastics and that the remediated soil remains safe and conducive for agricultural production.

articles.title:
Microplastics Are
Prevalent in Striped Bass and Shiner
Surfperch Tissues across San Francisco Bay, California
articles.abstract: Abstract The ingestion of microplastics by fish is widely documented, but the drivers of contamination and the movement of particles within organisms are still not well understood. We investigated microplastic contamination in sport fish caught from San Francisco Bay in California, USA. We compared microplastic contamination in striped bass (Morone saxatilis) and shiner surfperch (Cymatogaster aggregata). We observed an average of 5.9 ± 5.6 (Std Dev) microplastics per fish, with significantly higher overall contamination in striped bass but higher concentrations (microplastics/gram of tissue) in shiner surfperch. For each, we considered contamination relevant to their consumption by recreational anglers. For striped bass, where only the fillet is typically ingested, we found that contamination among tissues differed significantly (on average 3.8 ± 3.1 microplastics/fish fillets). Shiner surfperch, which are typically consumed whole, had an average body burden of 9.1 ± 1.2 microplastics/fish. Contamination varied significantly (p-value < 0.0001) among sampling locations for shiner surfperch, with the highest amounts observed near urban centers (no significant spatial pattern was observed for striped bass). Our findings show microplastics in tissues beyond the gastrointestinal tract, posing concerns for fish health and suggesting that fish caught from San Francisco Bay are a pathway for human consumption of microplastics.

articles.title:
Emerging Contaminants
Are Associated with Seasonal
Variations in Phytoplankton Community Diversity in a Eutrophic Lake
articles.abstract: Abstract Emerging contaminants (ECs) are increasingly detected in eutrophic lakes, yet their ecological contributions to phytoplankton community variation relative to conventional environmental factors remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the spatiotemporal occurrence of typical ECs and associated phytoplankton community variation in Taihu Lake, China. Phytoplankton abundance was significantly correlated with water temperature and total phosphorus (P < 0.05). Among the EC groups, organochlorine pesticides (37.7%), per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (16.7%), and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (16.1%) showed strong associations with the spatiotemporal variation in phytoplankton community composition. Organochlorine pesticides explained 18.8% and 25.9% of the α-diversity variation in spring and summer, respectively, and interaction analyses suggested potential combined effects among contaminant groups. Water quality factors and ECs jointly explained 67.9% of the community variation, with stronger associations observed in summer than in spring. Higher dominance of Cryptomonas ovata in Gonghu Bay during spring and Microcystis sp. in Western Bay during summer was associated with reduced phytoplankton community diversity under combined gradients of eutrophication and ECs. These findings highlight the covariation of phytoplankton communities with eutrophication and ECs and provide new insights into ecological risk assessment and algal bloom management in shallow eutrophic lakes.

articles.title:
Arsenate Adsorption
by Amorphous Titanium (Hydr)Oxides:
Governing Roles of Medium-Range Ordering and Surface Disorder
articles.abstract: Abstract Amorphous metal (hydr)oxides are used for oxyanion removal from water, yet the structural features responsible for their adsorption performance remain poorly understood. This paper systematically investigated how the ordering range and associated structural characteristics of amorphous titanium (hydr)oxides influence the adsorption of arsenate, used here as a model oxyanion. Six materials were synthesized with ordering ranges spanning approximately 4 to 43 Å. As the ordering range increased, a transition from microporous–mesoporous structures to predominantly mesoporous architectures was observed. Characterizations revealed progressive structural ordering with increasing synthesis aging temperature. The most amorphous sample exhibited stronger water binding, providing indirect evidence of fewer surrounding hydration clusters than in more ordered samples. However, despite possessing the highest specific surface area, the most amorphous material did not exhibit the highest arsenate uptake. Instead, the material aged at 140 °C achieved the greatest adsorption capacity, exceeding that of the fully amorphous material by >20%. This adsorption maximum coincided with an intermediate ordering range, a transitional structural state, and a mesopore-dominated pore architecture. The results indicate that arsenate adsorption is not governed by surface area alone. Instead, the ordering range provides a useful descriptor linking atomic-scale structure, pore architecture, hydration behavior, and adsorption performance in amorphous metal (hydr)oxides.

articles.title:
Dynamic
Hydrogen-Bonded
Hydration Networks Mitigate
Organic–Inorganic Fouling in Nanofiltration
articles.abstract: Abstract Hydration layers are widely recognized as the molecular basis of antifouling membrane interfaces, yet their role is still largely viewed through a static barrier picture. The dynamic response of hydrated membrane–water interfaces to approaching foulants, particularly under organic–inorganic mixed fouling conditions, remains poorly understood. Here, using poly(sulfobetaine methacrylate) (pSBMA)-modified nanofiltration membranes as a model zwitterionic interface, we reveal that fouling reversibility is strongly influenced by the dynamic stability of hydrogen-bonded hydration networks at the membrane–water interface. Molecular simulations combined with sum-frequency generation spectroscopy demonstrate that pSBMA sustains a strongly hydrogen-bonded interfacial water structure with preferential water dipole orientation under silicate and alginate perturbation, thereby suppressing long-lived foulant residence near the membrane surface. Real-time surface plasmon resonance measurements further confirm weakened irreversible foulant anchoring and enhanced interfacial reversibility. As a result, pSBMA-modified nanofiltration membranes reduced flux decline during mixed-foulant filtration to ∼6% and achieved >91% flux recovery after physical cleaning, accompanied by lower organic and inorganic foulant residuals. Repeated filtration–cleaning tests with real secondary effluent further confirmed nearly complete flux recovery in complex water matrices. These findings revisit zwitterionic antifouling by shifting the focus from static surface hydration to the dynamic stability of hydrogen-bonded hydration networks, providing a mechanistic basis for understanding and regulating fouling reversibility.

articles.title:
Unveiling Phase-Dependent
Fe–O Bond-Guided
Nitrate Reduction at Biocathodes: Balancing Interfacial Reactivity
and Iron Bioavailability
articles.abstract: Abstract Iron oxides are widespread in anoxic water environments, yet how their structures regulate microbial nitrate reduction remains unclear. Here, we reveal that phase-dependent Fe–O bond characteristics guide denitrification in bioelectrochemical system (BES) by balancing lattice-iron bioavailability and interfacial electrochemical reactivity at biocathodes. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that surface Fe–O bond covalency was associated with the thermodynamic barrier to lattice-iron release. α-Fe2O3, with the most negative ICOHP, exhibited the strongest Fe–O bonding and restricted iron release, thereby limiting microbial iron acquisition and downstream Fe–S cluster assembly. In contrast, γ-Fe2O3 and γ-FeOOH exhibited higher surface electroactivity but suffered from structural instability, evidenced by phase transformation, cell encrustation, and elevated microbial mortality. With mixed valence and balanced Fe–O bonding characteristics, Fe3O4 achieved the highest denitrification efficiency (17.8-fold enhancement over its abiotic control), which enabled direct Fe(II) uptake via the FeoAB system, bypassing siderophore-dependent acquisition and simultaneously activating both TonB-mediated iron acquisition and Fur-flavin-regulated respiratory pathways. This dual-pathway activation supported enhancement in biomass growth, intracellular electron transfer, and Fe–S cluster-dependent enzymatic activity. These findings help establish Fe–O bond characteristics as a key structural factor for Fe–N coupling and offer a structural perspective for rational design of iron-oxide-based nitrate-removal technologies.

articles.title:
A Perspective on
the Development of Novel In Situ
Remediation of Contaminated Sediments Using Black Carbon
articles.abstract: Abstract The field of contaminated sediment remediation was disrupted two decades ago by the emergence of a new way to reduce risk in situ through the amendment of black carbon sorbents─activated carbon and specialized biochars. This required a paradigm shift from a focus on reducing pollutant mass to reducing exposure through bioavailability control. Sorbent amendment technology has advanced from laboratory and pilot field demonstrations to full-scale applications at many sites and has recently been incorporated in USEPA records of decision at Superfund sites. This perspective summarizes critical points in advancing the new technology: 1) accurate problem definition recognizing that sediment pollutant mass reduction does not necessarily lead to risk reduction, 2) breakthroughs in bioavailability science and unraveling the role of native black carbon in sediments, 3) demonstration of pollutant bioavailability reduction with strong sorption, 4) quantitative descriptions of the process, 5) addressing the challenges of mercury, 6) understanding unintended consequences, and 7) development of freely dissolved concentrations as a key bioavailability metric with regulatory and stakeholder engagement. The lessons learned in this journey from early science through technological maturity can help inform other technologies that are in development to address evolving threats to the environment.

articles.title: Environmentally Persistent Free Radicals on Aged Polyamide Microplastics Drive Neurotoxicity in Eisenia fetida via a Glutamate-Centered Cascade
articles.abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-containing microplastics (N-MPs) are widespread in soil and often exhibit distinct environmental behaviors and effects owing to their unique elemental composition and molecular structure. However, their toxicity to soil organisms remains poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, the toxicity of pristine and aged polyamides (PA) was evaluated in earthworms (Eisenia fetida), a representative soil invertebrate. At 0.01% (w/w), aged PA increased the magnitude of body-weight loss, MDA levels, and AChE activity by 24.4%, 11.6%, and 24.1%, respectively, relative to pristine PA-MPs. Greater accumulation of aged PA-MPs was accompanied by enhanced oxidative damage and neurotoxicity. Integrated multiomics, quantitative real-time PCR, and biomarker analyses revealed that oxidative stress-mediated membrane damage promoted glutamate accumulation, receptor overactivation, Ca2+ overload, synaptic injury, and ultimately neurotoxicity. Pharmacological interventions and transmission electron microscopy of the ventral nerve cord provided functional and morphological support for this cascade. Radical quenching and comparative leachate bioassays further supported the important contribution of environmentally persistent free radicals in aged PA-MPs to neuronal damage. These findings define a mechanistic pathway for aged microplastic-induced neurotoxicity and provide a basis for assessing the ecological risks of aged N-MPs in soils.

articles.title:
Electrification,
Lightweighting, and Materials Supply:
A Dynamic Life Cycle Assessment of the U.S. Light-Duty Vehicle Fleet
articles.abstract: Abstract Electrification and lightweighting are reshaping vehicle designs and materials demand, with uncertain net effects on life cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Most existing fleet studies treat material choices, materials markets, and vehicle adoption separately, without capturing feedbacks between design, supply chains, and consumer behavior. This study develops an integrated system dynamics–life cycle assessment (SD–LCA) framework to explore these interactions for the U.S. light-duty vehicle fleet from 2000 to 2060. The model extends an established powertrain diffusion framework by endogenizing vehicle body material selection, battery capacity evolution, and materials market responses, linking these dynamics to a bottom-up life cycle assessment of fleet GHG emissions. Scenario analysis shows that increasing aluminum use in lightweight gasoline vehicles improves their utility and market share, largely offsetting use-phase GHG savings and yielding only modest reductions in total fleet emissions. In contrast, faster battery electric vehicle adoption raises cradle-to-gate emissions but more than compensates through lower use-phase emissions, reducing total fleet GHGs. Shifts in vehicle material demand also generate transient imbalances in steel and aluminum markets, temporarily lowering recycled fraction and increasing cradle-to-gate emissions. The SD–LCA framework demonstrates how feedbacks between vehicle design, materials supply, and consumer adoption shape fleet decarbonization pathways.

articles.title:
Trihalomethane Exposure,
Seminal Plasma Metabolomics,
and Semen Quality in Healthy Men: A Meet-in-the-Middle Approach
articles.abstract: Abstract Exposure to trihalomethanes (THMs) has been linked to reduced human semen quality, but the critical windows of vulnerability and underlying biological mechanisms remain unclear. We therefore measured untargeted seminal plasma metabolomics to identify metabolic biomarkers and biological pathways linking blood THM concentrations to repeated measurements of semen quality (4146 measurements over a 3 month follow-up period) among 762 healthy Chinese men. We found inverse associations between blood THM concentrations (i.e., chloroform, bromodichloromethane, and chlorinated THMs) and semen volume and total sperm count (all P values <0.05), which were most pronounced for exposure measured 70–90 days prior to semen collection (corresponding to the early stage of spermatogenesis). Metabolome-wide association analyses identified 90 metabolites that were simultaneously associated with blood THM concentrations and sperm-quality parameters. Mediation analyses further revealed that 44 metabolites, enriched in the pathways of unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis, steroid hormone biosynthesis, arachidonic acid metabolism, linoleic acid metabolism, pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis, and β-alanine metabolism, mediated a considerable proportion (8.1–41.3%) of the inverse relationships between THM exposure and semen quality. Our results suggest that THM exposure during the early stage of spermatogenesis is associated with reduced human semen quality, potentially driven by perturbations in lipid metabolism, steroid hormone synthesis, and antioxidant-related metabolisms.

articles.title:
Relative Humidity
Modulates Nitration and Ring Fragmentation
during Heterogeneous Oxidation of Catechol by Nitrate Radicals
articles.abstract: Abstract Catechol is an important biomass-burning-derived phenolic compound and a precursor to secondary organic aerosols (SOAs). Although nitrate radicals (NO3) are recognized as major nighttime oxidants, the influence of the aerosol water content on heterogeneous NO3 oxidation of phenolic compounds remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the impact of relative humidity (RH = 0–90%) on the heterogeneous oxidation of catechol thin films by nitrate radicals generated from the reaction of O3 and NO2. Product formation was characterized using Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, UV–visible spectroscopy, electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS), ultrahigh-pressure liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (UHPLC–MS), and ion chromatography–mass spectrometry (IC–MS). Under dry conditions, oxidation favored nitration and oligomerization pathways, producing mono-, di-, and trinitrocatechols together with catechol dimers and trimers. These products exhibited enhanced absorption in the 300–500 nm region, characteristic of brown carbon chromophores. Increasing RH progressively suppressed the relative nitration capacity of the NO3/N2O5 system while promoting oxidative ring-opening reactions, leading to the formation of dicarboxylic acids, including cis,cis-muconic acid, 2,3-dihydroxymaleic acid, and oxalic acid. Product distributions revealed a transition from functionalization-dominated chemistry at low RH to fragmentation-dominated chemistry at high RH. These results indicate that RH strongly controls nighttime nitrate radical oxidation of biomass-burning phenolics by shifting product formation from light-absorbing nitroaromatic brown carbon toward highly oxygenated fragmentation products. The findings provide new mechanistic insights into the role of aerosol water in governing the chemical aging and optical evolution of biomass-burning aerosols.

articles.title:
From
Molecular Topography
to Ozone Pollution: Species
Sources and Photochemical Kinetics of Individual Organic Peroxyl Radicals
articles.abstract: Abstract Ground-level ozone (O3) poses significant threats to global public health and climate change. Organic peroxyl radicals (RO2) serve as crucial intermediates in atmospheric O3 formation. Although individual RO2 species exhibit distinct reactivities, the quantification and source attribution of individual RO2 species remain poorly understood. Here, we address the challenge by integrating high-resolution field observations with fundamental theoretical kinetics within a novel hybrid receptor-kinetic modeling framework. The concentration and composition of RO2 species exhibit significant seasonal and diurnal dependencies. In summer, the 19 RO2 pool was characterized by a substantial contribution from biogenic sources (29%), particularly isoprene-derived species (ISOPOBO2). Conversely, the wintertime RO2 composition shifts, dramatically dominated by industrial emissions (41%), notably ethylene-derived species (HOCH2CH2O2). Source apportionment via the RO2+NO pathway further demonstrates that O3 photochemical formation potentials align closely with the kinetics of RO2 production. A data-driven machine learning model effectively captures the contribution of individual RO2 species to O3 formation in summer, but it shows significant deviations from kinetic simulations in winter. The framework establishes a dynamic framework to support daytime O3 mitigation by quantifying the high-time-resolution RO2 radical pool from field VOCs measurements.
